turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on some and any?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: use some in positive sentences, offers and requests; use any in negatives and most questions.
Right: "The farmer doesn't sell any milk." Wrong: "The farmer doesn't sell some milk." The sentence has doesn't, so it is negative and some does not fit.
My example: "The robot wants some paint." Step 1: I look for not or n't. There is none. Step 2: so it is positive. Step 3: I use some.
Now you try. Write some or any:
Sorry, we don't have ___ milk today.
